sync.title: Keeping Humans at the Center of AI
sync.rawTitle: #8 - Joan Clotet: Keeping Humans at the Center of AI | Leading in AI Podcast
sync.youtubeDescription:
Joan Clotet is a talent and leadership advisor, author, and podcast host who has spent nearly a decade building and championing the concept of Digital Humanism. With almost 40 years of experience inside organizations like Arthur Andersen, Ferrovial, and Grupo Zeta, Joan made the shift from IT consulting into talent and human resources before eventually going independent to work only with companies that genuinely invest in their people. He is the author of Humanismo Digital, a framework for keeping humans at the center of leadership decisions in an increasingly digital world.

In this episode, Joan shares the personal and professional origins of Digital Humanism, what it really means to become an independent advisor after decades inside large organizations, and how companies can help their people move from fearing AI to working alongside it. We also get into why empathy and context are the leadership skills AI can't replace, how to hire and manage "AI-augmented" junior talent, and his honest take on whether we'll ever see robots as our colleagues.

Topics covered:

- The origin story: How and why Joan coined "Digital Humanism" back in 2015
- Going independent: What it takes to "invent your own job" and only work with clients who value people
- Augmented, not automated: What "humans augmented by AI" really looks like inside a company
- The leadership skills AI can't replace: Empathy, context, and promoting change instead of just adapting to it
- Hiring the next generation: What it means to onboard "AI-augmented juniors"
- Robots as colleagues? Joan's take on AI-led companies and where he draws the line
